static_traits.name: Li Chen
static_traits.family_status: Living alone, no immediate family living together
static_traits.social_status: has a few casual acquaintances, but unwilling to discuss the 'luck' belief deeply with others, difficulty building deep relationships
static_traits.medical_history: no history of similar psychological problems; no past psychotherapy;No major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: High cooperativeness, clear expression, good logic, slightly nervous and able to notice and express emotions

basic_info.main_problem: I have always believed my children's books' success was just luck, negating my own efforts and talent.
basic_info.core_demands: I have noticed this thought is affecting my motivation to write and my overall well-being; I want to change this mindset and be able to feel proud of my work.
growth_experiences: three years ago after the first book unexpectedly went viral, the client began forming the belief that 'success comes from luck rather than ability'. Because success came quickly and unexpectedly, he struggles to attribute achievements to his own ability and effort, and this thought is repeatedly activated when Receiving compliments from others or seeing sales rise, accompanied by Anxiety,Self-doubt and guilt (feeling like 'taking credit for undeserved things'). Long-term pressure to keep producing new ideas,Decreased motivation, and emotional coping through excessive online shopping. The client is Living alone, with only a few casual acquaintances socially, difficulty building deep connections.

core_beliefs: I do not have enough ability/talent
my success does not belong to me (undeserved)

special_situations.event: When one's work is praised by others
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: if I attribute success to my own ability, it equals exaggerating myself and seems dishonest; only with fully certain evidence do I deserve recognition
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Downplays or avoids compliments, attributing success to 'luck', in order to reduce guilt and the pressure of being evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: this is just luck, not my ability.

special_situations.event: Seeing book sales rise or data performance improve
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: rising sales are accidental and unreplicable; if next time's results are not good it proves I have no ability
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: excessive worry, delaying writing investment, lowering expectations of outcomes for 'Self-protection'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: this time was just luck, next time I definitely cannot do it.

special_situations.event: When starting a new book and needing to propose new ideas
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: if I cannot think of better ideas, it means I have no talent; either excellent or a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: avoiding creation, distracting attention through online shopping to ease anxiety
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I have no talent at all, and will be seen through sooner or later.

special_situations.event: Recalls how the first success came quickly and unexpectedly
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: quick and unexpected success means mere chance, unrelated to ability; since it is chance, later success is also unreliable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: uniformly Interpreting success with 'luck', systematically negating one's own efforts and strengths
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: this is not truly my success.

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be seen and recognized as capable, hoping to feel proud of one's achievements
core_conflict.fear: fear of being seen through as a talentless 'impostor', worrying about being judged, criticized or negated by the next failure
defense_goal: Reduces the risk of being exposed by attributing success to luck
Avoiding acknowledging personal ability to reduce guilt and external expectations
Keeps a certain distance from others, avoiding talking about achievements to maintain a sense of safety

object_relations.self_representation: a person outwardly successful but inwardly undeserving, easily exposed
object_relations.object_representation: Others who may judge or expose oneself (even when they are praising)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When praised by others for his work, asked about reasons for success, or attention is paid to sales growth
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: understanding others' praise as excessive expectations or imminent scrutiny exposing oneself (transferentially Projecting the 'judge' onto others)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: repeatedly emphasizing 'luck/good timing' in a calm, understated tone, avoiding talk of ability and effort with objectifying words, and quickly Displacing to external factors (market, trends), reducing emotional expression.

manifestations: Attributes success mainly to luck, finding it hard to integrate achievements with the self, lacking pride and a sense of worth
A 'hollow feeling' from rapid success; hard to experience the meaning of effort and talent
outcomes: writing Decreased motivation,Decreased sense of happiness
Regulating emotions through excessive online shopping

manifestations: Living alone, social life mostly casual acquaintances
unwilling to discuss the 'luck' belief with others, difficulty building deep connections
outcomes: Weak support system; emotional burden is hard to be seen and carried
maintaining the Self-doubt and anxiety cycle

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Inwardly follows the implicit rule that 'only completely certain evidence deserves recognition'
tending to Interpret success as external chance, automatically negating self-contribution to avoid 'overstepping' or appearing arrogant

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Excessive scrutiny and harsh demands on one's own abilities, finding it hard to accept positive feedback
rising discomfort and tension when discussing achievements, tending to use external Interpretation to avoid self-disclosure

positive_force: Has creativity and children's literature expression ability (works are popular with child readers)
having Good self-awareness of the problem and actively seeking help,Positive attitude
able to identify and name negative automatic thought patterns (e.g. negating the positive, overgeneralization)
negative_force: Persistent self-doubt and 'impostor feelings', attributing success to luck
catastrophizing and predicting-the-future cognitive biases Reinforcing the Fear of failure and exposure
Avoidance and emotional coping (excessive online shopping) weaken sustained creation and motivation
Limited social support, hard to obtain emotional containment and reality correction from outside

target_behavior.behavior: attributing success to luck and systematically negating self-contribution (verbal and cognitive behaviors)
antecedent: Needing to come up with new ideas when starting a new project
target_behavior.core_reason: Fear of failure and being exposed as 'talentless' (impostor feelings) and cognitive biases like catastrophizing and overgeneralization
target_behavior.function: escaping self-worth evaluation and external expectations, thus temporarily reducing anxiety and guilt
target_behavior.consequence: writing motivation and Decline in sense of well-being, difficulty internalizing achievements and maintaining sustained output, deep relationship building blocked

target_behavior.behavior: Using excessive online shopping as emotional coping
antecedent: when creation is blocked and anxiety and guilt rise
when avoiding accepting praise or the discomfort after sales growth
target_behavior.core_reason: gaining short-term pleasure and distraction through instant Reinforcement, to avoid facing self-worth and creative pressure
target_behavior.function: gaining short-term emotional relief and attention Displacement (negative Reinforcement/positive Reinforcement)
target_behavior.consequence: time and energy consumed, core issues not yet addressed, avoidance and low-motivation patterns maintained
